keyPhrases.text: Herzog does what she accomplished in last year's rewrite of Ibsen's A Doll's House, which is to distill the play to its essence while setting up modern connections for today's audiences
Act I is pretty straightforward, even somewhat stiff
This is what the Herzog-Gold collaboration manages to do most effectively in the second half of the play
the production is filled with the kind of fiery and provocative speech
She clears the path in a way that allows us to readily imagine

reasoning: Review shows appreciation for Herzog's adaptation and the modern relevance created by the Herzog-Gold collaboration. While noting some stiffness in Act I, the critic praises the effectiveness of the second half and the contemporary connections. The tone is engaged and analytical rather than dismissive, with more positive observations than criticisms.
